bullets.text: Agency personal lines new business applications increased markedly with pleasing geographic dispersion; trailing three-month retention remained stubbornly slow, in contrast to Direct retention results and the Agency new business curve.
Companywide Q3 CR was just under 93; Commercial Lines produced an 85 CR; Property delivered a 92 CR, which included approximately 7 points of intangible asset amortization.
Commercial Lines premium grew 20%; Direct premium growth reached the low teens; Property premiums written were nearly $224M; Special lines premium grew around 2%.
Direct PIF grew around 8%; Agency auto remained not yet policy accretive to prior years; mix shifted to a higher composition of new business, requiring precise trend detection.
Loss frequency and other loss cost trends are definitely rising; multiple sources of inflation exist; Special lines experienced summer loss costs slightly lower than expectation without major storms.

Need for modest rate adjustments is building; adjusting pricing in smaller increments is preferred over delayed reactions; observed very definite competitor rate actions on personal auto across all means of distribution.

Platinum home and auto bundled offering rolled out past Texas into seven additional states, targeting Robinsons and future Robinsons through designated agents with very satisfactory early incremental growth.
Equity market was down and highly volatile during Q3; investment and capital strategy does not require rethinking positions or holding periods, leaving unrealized implications for portfolio results.

Seasonal potential for dramatic and impactful storms remained unrealized, though South Carolina experienced weather events; Special lines summer loss costs were slightly lower than expectation without major storms affecting boats or RVs.
Momentum credited to past actions; elevated CEO paranoia maintained to ensure sound decision-making; focus remains on future positioning and estimating prices for goods with unknown future costs.
